title: Bosphorus Bridges, Eurasia Tunnel & Marmaray: Understanding Istanbul Crossings
metaDescription: Compare Istanbul's 3 Bosphorus bridges, Eurasia Tunnel (330 TL), Marmaray rail, and ferries in 2026: speed, scenic views, and taxi vs transfer tolls.
quickAnswer: For crossing between Europe and Asia in Istanbul, Marmaray rail is fastest during rush hour (4 minutes undersea from Sirkeci to Üsküdar), the Eurasia Tunnel is quickest by private vehicle (330 TL daytime car toll in 2026), Şehir Hatları ferries (65.21 TL) are the most scenic, and the three road bridges cost 59–110 TL via HGS.

body.text: How do the 3 bridges, Eurasia car tunnel, Marmaray rail tunnel and ferries compare in speed?

Marmaray suburban rail crosses beneath the Bosphorus from Sirkeci to Üsküdar in roughly 4 minutes regardless of surface gridlock ([TCDD Taşımacılık](https://www.tcddtasimacilik.gov.tr/marmaray/tr/ucretlendirme)). By car, the [Eurasia Tunnel](https://www.avrasyatuneli.com/en/tolls/) cuts the Kazlıçeşme–Göztepe run to about 15 minutes, whereas the 15 July Martyrs and Fatih Sultan Mehmet bridges can stretch past 60 minutes at rush hour.

body.text: When does the Eurasia Tunnel save 45+ minutes for private transfers?

The Eurasia Tunnel routinely saves 45 to 60 minutes on weekday afternoons (16:00–20:30) and rainy Friday evenings when traveling between the Historic Peninsula (Sultanahmet, Karaköy, Yenikapı) and Asian-side hubs like Kadıköy, Ataşehir, or Sabiha Gökçen Airport (SAW). Because it bypasses the 15 July Martyrs Bridge approaches, traffic keeps moving steadily beneath the seabed.

As of July 1, 2026, the official [Eurasia Tunnel](https://www.avrasyatuneli.com/en/news-and-announcements/detail/eurasia-tunnel-toll-rates-as-of-1-july-2026) daytime tariff (05:00–23:59) is 330 TL for Class 1 cars and 495 TL for Class 2 minibuses (such as Mercedes Vito/Sprinter airport vans), dropping 50% between 00:00 and 04:59 to 165 TL and 247.50 TL. In winter rain or fog—when surface bridges stall and ferries occasionally pause—the tunnel is the single most predictable road link; check our [Türkiye winter travel guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/turkey-in-winter-premium-travel-guide) for cold-weather transfer buffers.
Which crossing is most scenic for first-time visitors?

Nothing matches the open upper deck of a public [Şehir Hatları ferry](https://sehirhatlari.istanbul/en/price-list) from Eminönü or Karaköy to Kadıköy, or from Beşiktaş to Üsküdar. In 20 minutes you pass Topkapı Palace, Maiden's Tower, and the Galata skyline for 65.21 TL—far better views than any highway lane or underground rail tube.

Time your ferry crossing for late afternoon (30 minutes before sunset) heading from Kadıköy back to Karaköy so the sun lights up Sultanahmet's domes behind you. Buy a glass of hot tea on board from the ferry canteen, sit outdoors on the stern bench, and skip private "shortcut" motorboats unless you are racing a fixed restaurant reservation. If you plan to continue south across the Sea of Marmara by fast ferry, pair your Asian-side afternoon with our [Bursa destination guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/destinations/bursa).
How do tolls apply to taxis vs private transfers?

Yellow Istanbul taxis pass the exact bridge or Eurasia Tunnel toll directly to the passenger on top of the metered fare—there are no cash booths, as every crossing reads the vehicle's HGS transponder electronically ([KGM Tolls](https://www.kgm.gov.tr/Sayfalar/KGM/SiteEng/Root/Tolls.aspx)). Pre-booked private transfers typically include standard bridge tolls in the quoted rate, while Eurasia Tunnel fees are either bundled or billed explicitly at cost.
Use this checklist before stepping into any intercontinental vehicle:

items: Ask before entering the tunnel: Tell your taxi driver clearly if you want the Eurasia Tunnel (330 TL extra) rather than a 59 TL bridge.

Verify two-way bridge charging: All three Bosphorus bridges charge in both directions since 2022, so every crossing triggers a separate toll ([Vignetim](https://vignetim.com/blog/istanbul-bridge-tolls)).
Confirm Vito/Sprinter vehicle class: Minibuses pay Class 2 rates (495 TL in the Eurasia Tunnel; 75 TL on the first two bridges), not sedan rates.
Keep small bills or card ready: Confirm before departing whether your taxi accepts contactless cards, especially for airport runs.
Avoid paying return tolls: You only owe the toll for the direction you actually ride in—never let a driver double-charge for their empty return leg.

faq.q: How much is the Eurasia Tunnel toll in 2026?
faq.a: As of July 1, 2026, daytime tolls (05:00–23:59) are 330 TL for cars (Class 1) and 495 TL for minibuses (Class 2). Night tolls (00:00–04:59) are discounted by 50% to 165 TL for cars and 247.50 TL for minibuses.

faq.q: Do Bosphorus bridges charge tolls in both directions?
faq.a: Yes. All three road bridges—15 July Martyrs, Fatih Sultan Mehmet, and Yavuz Sultan Selim—charge per crossing in both the Europe-to-Asia and Asia-to-Europe directions via automated HGS plate scanning.

faq.q: How long does Marmaray take to cross between Europe and Asia?
faq.a: The undersea rail segment between Sirkeci (Europe) and Üsküdar (Asia) takes approximately 4 minutes, making it the fastest way to cross during peak weekday rush hour.

faq.q: Can tour buses use the Eurasia Tunnel or 15 July Martyrs Bridge?
faq.a: No. Full-size coaches and heavy trucks are prohibited from both the Eurasia Tunnel and the 15 July Martyrs Bridge; they must use the northern Yavuz Sultan Selim Bridge.

faq.q: Can you walk across any of the Bosphorus bridges?
faq.a: No. Pedestrian access is closed on all three Bosphorus bridges for safety, except during the annual Istanbul Marathon when the 15 July Martyrs Bridge opens briefly to runners.

faq.q: Does an İstanbulkart work on both Marmaray and Şehir Hatları ferries?
faq.a: Yes. One İstanbulkart covers Marmaray trains, Şehir Hatları ferries, metro lines, and trams; on Marmaray, tap out at the exit refund machines to recover any unused distance deposit.
